guide_title: Metro Solid Waste & Resource Recovery Handbook (2026 Edition)
jurisdiction: Metro Municipal Solid Waste Authority (Single-Stream & Drop-Off)
coverage_summary: Covers household rigid plastics (#1, #2, #5), glass containers, clean paper/cardboard, metal cans, multi-layer beverage cartons, compostable organics, and household hazardous/e-waste.
unverified_scope: Industrial chemicals, medical sharps, construction rubble, and unmarked composite bio-plastics.

passages.section: Section 4.1 — Rigid Household Plastics (#1 PET, #2 HDPE, #5 PP)
required_conditions: Container must be empty, rinsed free of food residue, and dry.
Black carbon-pigmented plastic is NOT accepted by optical sorters.
preparation_steps: Empty all liquid or food residue completely.
Give a quick rinse and shake dry.
Replace plastic screw caps tightly onto the bottle before placing in the Blue Bin.
passages.exceptions: Black microwave trays, foam polystyrene (#6 EPS), and flexible film pouches must go to General Waste.
passages.excerpt: Clean rigid plastic bottles, tubs, and jugs bearing resin identification codes #1 (PET), #2 (HDPE), and #5 (PP) are accepted in curbside Dry Recyclables. Carbon-black plastics belong in General Waste.

required_conditions: Must be food or beverage packaging glass (clear, green, or amber).
Must not be heat-treated borosilicate (Pyrex), mirror, window glass, or ceramics.
preparation_steps: Rinse jar or bottle clean; paper labels may remain attached.
Remove metal lids and recycle them separately in the Metal stream.
passages.exceptions: Drinking glasses, Pyrex bakeware, and lightbulbs contaminate glass cullet.
passages.excerpt: Clear, green, and amber food and beverage bottles and jars are 100% recyclable in the Glass stream. Separate metal lug caps into dry mixed recycling. Never include heat-resistant borosilicate glass.

required_conditions: Material must be dry and free from soaked grease, oil, or food residue.
Must not have plastic film lamination or metallic foil coating.
preparation_steps: Remove all inner plastic air pillows and foam inserts.
Flatten boxes completely to conserve collection capacity.
Tear off and compost or discard heavily greased sections (such as pizza box bottoms).
passages.exceptions: Greasy paper and wax-coated produce boxes contaminate paper pulp.
passages.excerpt: Clean, dry corrugated cardboard and uncoated paperboard boxes belong in Clean Fiber recycling. Flatten all boxes. Tear off greasy sections before recycling.

required_conditions: Never place in curbside recycling or general waste bins due to severe lithium fire hazard.
preparation_steps: Tape the terminals of lithium-ion and 9V batteries with clear non-conductive tape.
Deliver to a municipal E-Waste kiosk or retail take-back drop box.
passages.exceptions: Swollen or damaged lithium batteries must be placed in a non-flammable container with sand.
passages.excerpt: MANDATORY SAFETY RULE: Batteries, power banks, charging cords, and small electronics are strictly banned from curbside bins. Tape battery terminals and bring to an authorized E-Waste Drop-Off.

required_conditions: Container must be completely empty and rinsed.
preparation_steps: Empty contents and rinse food residue.
passages.exceptions: Pressurized aerosols and paint cans with wet residue are excluded.
passages.excerpt: Empty aluminum beverage cans, steel food tins, and clean aluminum foil balls are accepted in Dry Recyclables.
